claim: Backup policies are merged only when they share the same backup plan name; otherwise policies can coexist in an account without merging.
question: When are Organizations backup policies merged into one effective plan?

values.display: only for backup policies that share the same backup plan name
coexist in that account without any merging

evidence.quote: Merging is done only for backup policies that share the same backup plan name. You can also have policy A and policy B coexist in that account without any merging.

claim: Continuous backup first creates a full backup of the resource and then constantly backs up its transaction logs; point-in-time recovery replays the transaction log on the full backup to the time you choose.
question: How do continuous backups and point-in-time recovery work in AWS Backup?

values.display: constantly backing up your resource's transaction logs
replaying the transaction log to the time

evidence.quote: Continuous backup works by first creating a full backup of your resource, and then constantly backing up your resource’s transaction logs. PITR works by accessing your full backup and replaying the transaction log to the time that you tell AWS Backup to recover.

claim: With continuous backups you can restore a supported resource by rewinding it to a specific time you choose, to within 1 second of precision, going back a maximum of 35 days.
question: How precise is a point-in-time restore from continuous backups and how far back can it go?

values.display: within 1 second of precision
a maximum of 35 days

evidence.quote: With continuous backups, you can restore your AWS Backup-supported resource by rewinding it back to a specific time that you choose, within 1 second of precision (going back a maximum of 35 days).

claim: Because continuous and snapshot backups offer different advantages, AWS recommends protecting resources with both continuous and snapshot backup rules.
question: Should a resource have a continuous backup rule, a snapshot rule, or both?

values.display: both continuous and snapshot backup rules
different advantages

evidence.quote: Because continuous and snapshot backups offer different advantages, we recommend that you protect your resources with both continuous and snapshot backup rules.

claim: An on-demand backup begins to back up your resource immediately, and you can use it to create a backup at a time other than the schedule of a backup plan.
question: When does an on-demand backup start and what is it for?

values.display: begins to back up your resource immediately
other than the scheduled time defined in a backup plan

evidence.quote: An on-demand backup begins to back up your resource immediately. You can choose an on-demand backup if you wish to create a backup at a time other than the scheduled time defined in a backup plan. An on-demand backup can be used, for example, to test backup and functionality at any time.

claim: You cannot use on-demand backups with point-in-time recovery, because an on-demand backup preserves the resource's state at one moment while PITR uses continuous backups that record changes over a period of time.
question: Can an on-demand backup be a continuous (PITR) backup?

values.display: can't use on-demand backups with PITR
record changes over a period of time

evidence.quote: You can't use on-demand backups with PITR, because an on-demand backup preserves resources in the state they are in when the backup is taken, while PITR uses continuous backups, which record changes over a period of time.

claim: A continuous backup plan creates one continuous recovery point and updates that recovery point whenever the job runs.
question: How many recovery points does a continuous backup plan create?

values.display: creates one continuous recovery point
updates that recovery point whenever the job runs

evidence.quote: You can opt in to continuous backups for supported resources when you create a backup plan in AWS Backup using the AWS Backup console or the API. The continuous backup plan creates one continuous recovery point and updates that recovery point whenever the job runs.

claim: Each resource can have only one continuous backup (recovery point); additional continuous backups are redundant.
question: How many continuous backups can one resource have?

values.display: can only have one continuous backup
additional continuous backups are redundant

evidence.quote: Each resource (such as an Amazon S3 bucket or an Amazon RDS database) can only have one continuous backup (recovery point); additional continuous backups are redundant.

claim: If several rules specify more than one continuous backup in a single vault, AWS Backup follows the rule with the longest retention period and ignores the additional rules.
question: Which rule wins when several rules ask for a continuous backup of one resource in one vault?

values.display: follows the rule with the longest retention period
ignores additional rules

evidence.quote: If multiple rules specify that more than one continuous backup should be in a single vault, AWS Backup follows the rule with the longest retention period (lifecycle) and ignores additional rules.

claim: If rules specify continuous backups of one resource in more than one vault, AWS Backup creates one continuous backup under the first rule processed, and each later continuous rule for that resource results in a snapshot (periodic) backup instead.
question: What happens when continuous backup rules for one resource point at different vaults?

values.display: creates one continuous backup according to the first rule processed
will result in a snapshot (periodic) backup instead

evidence.quote: If multiple rules specify that more than one continuous backup should be in more than one vault, AWS Backup creates one continuous backup according to the first rule processed. Each subsequent rule specifying a continuous backup for a resource that already has a continuous backup will result in a snapshot (periodic) backup instead.

claim: AWS Backup for S3 relies on S3 events delivered through Amazon EventBridge; if that setting is disabled in the S3 bucket notification settings, continuous backups stop for those buckets.
question: What stops S3 continuous backups if it is turned off?

values.display: relies on receiving S3 events through Amazon EventBridge
continuous backups will stop

evidence.quote: AWS Backup for S3 relies on receiving S3 events through Amazon EventBridge. If this setting is disabled in S3 bucket notification settings, continuous backups will stop for those buckets with the setting turned off.

claim: AWS Backup supports continuous backups and point-in-time recovery for all RDS instances and Aurora that the native RDS service supports, but not for Amazon RDS Multi-AZ clusters.
question: Does AWS Backup support continuous backups for RDS Multi-AZ clusters?

values.display: does not support continuous backups or point-in-time recovery for Amazon RDS Multi-AZ clusters
all Amazon RDS instances and Aurora

evidence.quote: AWS Backup supports continuous backups and point-in-time recovery for all Amazon RDS instances and Aurora that are supported by the native Amazon RDS service. AWS Backup does not support continuous backups or point-in-time recovery for Amazon RDS Multi-AZ clusters.

claim: While AWS Backup manages continuous backups for an RDS instance you cannot configure the automated backup window directly; AWS Backup places it near the RDS maintenance window, and you can influence the placement by adjusting the RDS maintenance window.
question: Can you set the RDS automated backup window while AWS Backup manages continuous backups?

values.display: cannot directly configure the automated backup window
positions this automated backup window near the Amazon RDS maintenance window

qualifiers.scope: RDS instances with AWS Backup continuous backups

evidence.quote: AWS Backup positions this automated backup window near the Amazon RDS maintenance window to prevent conflicts. You cannot directly configure the automated backup window while AWS Backup manages continuous backups, but you can influence its placement by adjusting your Amazon RDS maintenance window.
